title: Compact quant kernel nucleus batcher and KV-window harmonizer
author: Marco Ruiz
release_notes: Introduces Compact Quant Kernel with nucleus batcher and KV-window harmonizer to improve INT8/FP8 throughput and reduce p95 latency for quantized models. Backwards compatible; opt-in via runtime flags. Can be rolled out via canary on Dedicated clusters.
description:
Motivation: We see recurrent tokenization and KV copy overheads when serving quantized (INT8/FP8) models under mixed sequence-length workloads. Existing continuous-batching strategies over-aggregate tokens and cause per-head re-quantization churn, which increases tail latency and memory churn during KV cache flushes. This PR implements a compact quant execution path plus a new 'nucleus batcher' that selectively coalesces token work by locality and per-head scale compatibility, and a KV-window harmonizer that aligns KV slice boundaries to micro-batches to avoid extra copies.

Design summary: - Compact Quant Kernel: fused scale-folding + zero-point elimination path that avoids separate dequant/requant stages for a common subset of int8/FP8 kernels. The kernel exposes a narrow API surface so runtime can swap it based on per-model quant metadata. - Nucleus Batcher: continuous batching policy that groups outstanding tokens not purely by arrival time but by compatibility of quantization scales and target sequence window. It keeps micro-batches small for latency-critical tails while batching compatible tokens for throughput. - KV-window Harmonizer: coordinates micro-batch KV read/write ranges so that KV cache windows are aligned across coalesced micro-batches. This reduces memcpy churn and allows zero-copy KV references on supported hardware.

Implementation notes: - runtime/quant/compact_kernel.cpp/h: new fused paths with safe fallbacks to existing dequant->float->kernel path. - runtime/scheduler/nucleus_batcher.cpp: scheduling policy implementation, metrics, and config knobs. - runtime/kv/kv_window_harmonizer.cpp: alignment logic and compatibility checks. - tests/benchmark/quant_nucleus_bench.py: microbench harness for seq_len = [64, 512, 1024], batch = [1..16], measuring throughput and p50/p95. - docs/perf/quant-batcher.md: design doc and rollout instructions.

Performance: Benchmarked on r5-gpu (NVIDIA L4 equiv) with a 7B quantized model (INT8+smoothquant profile): - End-to-end throughput: +22% at batch=8, seq=512. - p95 latency: -11% for mixed arrival workloads (Poisson token arrivals). - Memory copies: KV memcpy reduced ~37% for micro-batched coalesces. For FP8 models we see a 12-18% throughput uplift depending on headwise scale variability.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated behind runtime flag (quant.compact_path = true). 2) Canary deploy to 1% of Hosted and one Dedicated customer for 48h, monitor metrics: token_throughput, p95_latency, kv_memcpy_bytes. 3) Gradual ramp with automatic rollback on quality regressions.

Compatibility and risks: - Not enabled for models that set per-layer custom dequant hooks; in those cases runtime falls back to the stable path. - Risk: small numeric differences in rare edge cases due to fused scale folding; mitigated by unit tests and end-to-end evals on our validation prompt sets.

Checklist:
- [x] Compact kernel implementation with tests
- [x] Nucleus batcher policy and config
- [x] KV-window harmonizer and integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks and docs
- [x] Canary rollout plan

Related: ENG-4291 (quant pipeline efficiency), ENG-4328 (continuous batching experiment).
